course_name_en: Chemical Reactor Engineering and Bioreactor Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Design (dimensioning) and analyze the operation of chemical reactors, mainly stationary, but also with attention to transient behavior.
Develop a formalism using mass and energy balances to design homogeneous reactors for different ideal reactor prototypes, then extend it to heterogeneous reactions.
Understand the influence of the type of reaction kinetics on the yield and/or selectivity of the produced products.

syllabus_topics: Introduction
Problem statement and description of ideal reactor prototypes
Comparison between batch and continuous reactors, tubular and tank reactor
Discussion of other industrial reactor types
Fundamentals
Concepts of reaction rate, kinetics, conversion, chemical equilibrium, heat of reaction
Formulation of mass and enthalpy balances
Isothermal homogeneous reactor systems
Design and analysis based on mass balance for batch reactor, perfect mixer, plug flow reactor, recycle reactor
Combinations of ideal reactors: mixers in series (cascade arrangement), optimal tank and tube combination
Transient cascade: flushing and cleaning operations
Temperature effects in homogeneous reactors
Design and analysis based on coupled mass and heat balance, discussion of reactor prototypes with heat exchange, optimal temperature profile for reversible reaction
Study of the non-isothermal tank reactor: stationary design, analysis of multiplicity, stability of operation and transient behavior
Non-ideal flow in reactors
Residence time distribution (RTD) in reactors: definition, mathematical description and experimental determination (signal-response techniques)
Residence time distribution derived from a priori known flow in reactor
Calculation of conversion in non-ideal reactors by using RTD-info
Heterogeneous catalytic reactions
Study of external mass and heat transport in combination with chemical reaction
Transport in porous catalyst with simultaneous chemical reaction
Catalyst effectiveness factor, design of heterogeneous reactors
Chemical kinetics
Analysis and processing of kinetic measurements
Influence of kinetics on selectivity and yield for complex reactions

assessment_methods.method: Written preparation with oral explanation (theory part)
1 to 2 numerical exercise problems (exercises part), fully written

assessment_rules: For the theory part, the exam is closed book (only the formularium may be used), with written preparation followed by an oral explanation. For the exercises part, there will be 1 to 2 numerical exercise problems, open book, with a fully written evaluation.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
